fact_text: Enterprise value equals market capitalisation plus total debt minus cash and cash equivalents, giving the theoretical cost of acquiring the whole company.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Enterprise Value (EV) Explained | EV/Sales | EV/EBITDA | Part 06 | Learn Fundamental Analysis |PSX' (YouTube, 2026-03-07)

fact_text: Market capitalisation is the current share price multiplied by the total outstanding shares.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Enterprise Value (EV) Explained | EV/Sales | EV/EBITDA | Part 06 | Learn Fundamental Analysis |PSX' (YouTube, 2026-03-07)

fact_text: Debt is added to market cap because a buyer of the whole company also takes on its obligations, while cash is deducted because it becomes the buyer's own working capital.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Enterprise Value (EV) Explained | EV/Sales | EV/EBITDA | Part 06 | Learn Fundamental Analysis |PSX' (YouTube, 2026-03-07)

fact_text: Enterprise value per share is enterprise value divided by total shares outstanding; comparing it with the share price shows how far debt and cash move value away from the market price.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Enterprise Value (EV) Explained | EV/Sales | EV/EBITDA | Part 06 | Learn Fundamental Analysis |PSX' (YouTube, 2026-03-07)

fact_text: EV to sales divides enterprise value by sales; the analyst said it helps mainly in comparing companies within a peer group rather than as a stand-alone signal.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Enterprise Value (EV) Explained | EV/Sales | EV/EBITDA | Part 06 | Learn Fundamental Analysis |PSX' (YouTube, 2026-03-07)

fact_text: EV to EBITDA divides enterprise value by EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation), and is used to compare operating efficiency across peers.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Enterprise Value (EV) Explained | EV/Sales | EV/EBITDA | Part 06 | Learn Fundamental Analysis |PSX' (YouTube, 2026-03-07)

fact_text: Buying 100% of a listed company at market price is rarely possible, because most shares are not on the market and control deals are usually struck off-market.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Enterprise Value (EV) Explained | EV/Sales | EV/EBITDA | Part 06 | Learn Fundamental Analysis |PSX' (YouTube, 2026-03-07)

fact_text: The analyst cited Mian Mansha's takeover of Adamjee Insurance as an example of a hostile takeover in Pakistan, which he said was the first such case in the country.
